title: The observations of a project record that name the producer's machine and not the project's inputs
description: A stored project record carries every filesystem fact its inference consumed, and a taker replays them against its own tree before it uses the record. Two kinds of fact name the producer's machine and not an input: (1) `lstat` of every directory above the checkout (`/`, `/Users`, `/Users/Shared`, or `/home`, `/home/deck`: the realpath walk of the TypeScript compiler), which holds on no machine with another checkout location, and (2) every path below `.cache/b/d/m/j/<id>/`, the dependency generation the inference tooling ran from (its id derives from the checkout and the platform, and every record holds exactly one). Measured on 2870 production records: 1824 of 1825 macOS records and 545 of 546 Linux records hold both kinds, so before this module a record produced under one checkout could not hold under another, and never on another platform. A record is published portable: the location rows are dropped (a directory above the checkout exists whenever the checkout does, so the fact cannot decide anything) and the generation id is replaced by a token; the taker puts its own generation in the token's place (the real path of its `node_modules`), so the rows are replayed against the tooling it runs from, whose identity the `field` row of the compiler (a package identity digest) still decides. A record that holds several generation ids, or a taker that has no generation, keeps rows that cannot hold, and the project is inferred locally.
